correctness.rationale: For a²≠4, t²+at+1 has distinct nonzero roots so x^10+a x^5+1 is squarefree of degree ten. The p=7 Cartier–Manin coefficient matrix has four-cycle entries M12=M43=3a and M24=M31=3(a²+1); all four nonzero iff ordinary, otherwise two nonzero yield rank two/a-number two and nilpotent semilinear iteration hence p-rank zero. These rank calculations alone do NOT prove supersingularity. Independent F7^4 enumeration of ALL 2401 x showed for a=0 and i²=-1 exactly 10 roots,1391 nonzero square values,1000 nonsquares; with two infinity points this gives #=2794, equality in Weil bound q+1+8sqrt(q), forcing all Frobenius eigenvalues -49 over F2401 and Newton slope 1/2. The low-degree counts and functional equation give (1+49T⁴)^2 over F7 for a=0, and equal sign multiplicities over F49 give (1+49T²)^4 for both. Geometric two-class count uses the cited Ohashi–Kudo parameter symmetry; no claim about arithmetic twists.
residual_risks: Full exceptional point census reproduced; p-rank classification for arbitrary algebraic closure uses symbolic Cartier support, not the finite enumeration.
